name: Herveus Burgidolensis
claimNotes: Entire corpus untranslated. Known for Commentarii in Isaiam prophetam (Isaiah commentary) and other biblical exegesis.

name: Isidorus Mercator
claimNotes: Entire Pseudo-Isidorian Decretals collection remains untranslated. Best Latin edition is Hinschius (1863) but no complete English translation exists.

name: Carolus Magnus
claimNotes: All works (primarily capitularies, letters, decrees)

name: Sicardus Cremonensis
claimNotes: Mitrale, sive De officiis ecclesiasticis summa (comprehensive liturgical treatise, 9 books).

name: Rodulfus Trudonis
claimNotes: Gesta abbatum Trudonensium (historiographical account of abbots of St. Trond in seven books)—entirely in Latin.

name: Christianus Druthmarus
claimNotes: Expositio in Matthaeum (Commentary on Matthew), biblical commentaries

name: Wilhelmus Hirsaugiensis
claimNotes: Writings on music and astronomy, commentaries

name: Algerus Leodiensis
claimNotes: De misericordia et iustitia and De sacramento remain in Latin; studied through Latin editions only

name: Henricus de Castro Marsiaco
claimNotes: Henry of Marcy's important anti-heretical writings on Catharism and Waldensianism remain largely in Latin

name: Jacobus Caietanus
claimNotes: Giacomo Gaetani Stefaneschi's Opus Metricum (verse life of Celestine V, the earliest biography of the hermit-pope) has no identified English translation

name: Godefridus Viterbiensis
claimNotes: Pantheon and Chronicon - chronicles of world history to 1186 - remain in Latin

name: Richerus S. Remigii
claimNotes: Chronicle of Richer of Reims remains untranslated; important medieval historical source

name: Gualterus de Castellione
claimNotes: Alexandreis (epic of Alexander the Great) untranslated; medieval literary significance unmatched

name: Herbertus Turrium in Sardinia
claimNotes: Fragmenta ex libris de miraculis Cisterciensium monachorum (fragments on Cistercian miracles) untranslated; appears in PL 185

name: Amulo Lugdunensis
claimNotes: Sententiae ex libris Augustini and other theological works remain untranslated

name: Anselmus Lucensis
claimNotes: Collectio canonum (1081-1083), Liber contra Wibertum; important Gregorian Reform canonical works

name: Thiofridus Efternacensis
claimNotes: Flores epytaphii sanctorum (c. 1104/5) on relics; hagiographical works; no English translation located

name: Usuardus Sangermanensis
claimNotes: Martyrologium (c. 875); 1100+ saints' lives; became basis for Roman Martyrology; no complete English translation located

name: Joannes Venetus
claimNotes: Istoria Veneticorum (c. 1008), first history of Venice; no English, French, or international translation published

name: Aimoinus Sangermanensis
claimNotes: Gesta Francorum, Historia Francorum (Libri V), Vita Abbonis (9th–10th c.); no English translation located
